explanation: Its blood cells clot around traces of bacterial toxins, so drug makers have long used them to check for contamination. Horseshoe crabs are closer to spiders and scorpions than to true crabs.

claims.text: Blood from horseshoe crabs has been used for decades to make a test (LAL) that checks vaccines, injectable drugs and medical devices for bacterial endotoxins.
Octopus, lobster and squid blood is also blue but is not used to test medicines for bacterial toxins.
Horseshoe crab blood cells (amebocytes) clot in the presence of bacterial endotoxins.
Horseshoe crabs are chelicerates, more closely related to spiders and scorpions than to true crabs.

evidence.restatement: Limulus amebocyte lysate (LAL), made from horseshoe crab blood, has been used since the 1970s to test injectable drugs, vaccines and devices for bacterial endotoxin.
Octopus, squid and lobster blood is also blue (haemocyanin), but it is not the basis of the endotoxin test.
Horseshoe crab amebocytes clot when they meet bacterial endotoxin.
Horseshoe crabs are chelicerates, closer to spiders and scorpions than to true crabs.
Horseshoe crab blood is the basis of the LAL clotting test, used for decades to screen vaccines, injectable drugs and devices for bacterial endotoxin.
Octopus, squid and lobster blood is also blue (copper-based haemocyanin) but is not used in endotoxin tests.
Horseshoe crab blood cells (amebocytes) clot when bacterial endotoxin is present.
Horseshoe crabs are chelicerates, nearer to spiders and scorpions than to true crabs.

issues.note: The explanation says drug makers use the clotting test in the present tense. That is true today, but recombinant alternatives now exist and may displace horseshoe crab blood over time, so the present tense could age. The stem ("has been used for decades") is safe; consider "have used" in the explanation.
